answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, externally acquired bond before it may post jobs or claim rewards. A challenge period lets peers flag linked identities; proven fraud burns the bond and returns part to reporters, while honest accounts unlock it after settlement. This makes a terrace of disposable personas costly: the attacker must buy and immobilize capital per identity, and a ripple of detected accounts can expose shared funding. Nectar-like rewards should accrue only after verified work, not account creation.
